text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR Cable Modem CM500 - Compatible with all Cable Providers incl. Xfinity, Spectrum, Cox | For Cable Plans up to 400Mbps | DOCSIS 3.0 Comcast has repeatedly lied to me, sending me letters and alerts telling me that I need a new cable modem or my service will be seriously degraded. One time they went so far as to set a date when my service would NO longer work at all! Of course, I would never believe them without double-checking for myself, and I found out it was indeed an outright lie. Even the oldest DOCSIS versions can handle more than my 30Mbps connection. I suppose the lie was because they want me to rent their modem for $10 or more a month and relinquish control of my own network to them.

That said, it makes sense to upgrade when convenient to be sure you're future proofed. Eventually even the cheapest Internet plans will be upgraded to higher speeds. When I heard that I could register this on Comcast's network online without having to call them (and have them speak extremely condescendingly to me even though I'm a Systems Engineer), I was sold. Worth doing.

Note that just because DOCSIS 3.0 can reach speeds of 10Gbps with maxed out number of channels, this modem is 680Mbps, which will be out of date eventually, when we finally get Gigabit Ethernet to residences.

Another (of a million) thing(s) I hate about Comcast is that they by default use your AP (that they rent to you as part of a router/AP/modem combo) to create a public (virtual) wireless AP for their other customers. They say this will not affect your bandwidth, but it can affect your throughput. And it uses your electricity. And why would you want to help Comcast, when they take advantage of you any chance they can.

Point of all this is me encouraging you to get your own modem, get your own router and AP (or combo unit, although I prefer them separate) and pare down your ISP bill as much as you can. Stop giving them money.

Note that apparently if you get voice service through Comcast, you'll still need their combo modem unit of some sort. Well, cut that service from your monthly budget too. If we just had some competition, I'd cut Comcast out of my life completely.

Another thing is that if you have their modem and you need help with it, they may call it your responsibility and charge you for any "help" they provide. At least if you own your own stuff, you'll know if it's your problem or theirs.

Modem is straightforward and easy to use as any. If you ever download at high rates for days on end, it'll need cycled, but that's not the modem's fault; it just happens.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Cable Modem CM500 - Compatible with all Cable Providers incl. Xfinity, Spectrum, Cox | For Cable Plans up to 400Mbps | DOCSIS 3.0

Then plug in the second router on the other side of your house and run the Google Home app to add that device.

text_fidelity_a: SAMSUNG 34-Inch Odyssey G85SB Series QD-OLED Ultra WQHD Curved Gaming Monitor, 175Hz, 0.03ms, DisplayHDR True Black 400, AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, Advanced Game Streaming, LS34BG850SNXZA, 2023 Putting together this beast was not a very difficult task.  I am using the 'Ergotron – HX Single Ultrawide Monitor Arm' with this monitor.  There was a little bit of an odd feeling when it took me hooking both hdmi and display port up to figure out how to deal with the monitor source correctly.  This overall though is the most amazing monitor I've ever sat in front of.  I use this for engineering work as I'm not a gamer.  The screen real estate is much larger than typical 4k 1440p monitors.  The jump from a 34" to 49" was not as drastic of an impression as I would have expected.  The curve softens the hit to the senses as it seems a little shorter than it actually is.  The curve takes a little getting used to but it's not near as aggressive as people claim.  This is my first curved monitor because I didn't know if I could get used to it or not.  After a few hours of working on it, I barely notice anymore.  The picture is very clean and crisp.  I'm using it in conjunction with a sapphire card.  There are plenty of reviews about the exact specs of this monitor, but really I wanted to note that it shines when it comes to just immersing someone into the screen.  I only would suggest this to people that have a very deep measuring desk because this does take up quite a lot of room over the desk even with an arm holding it up.  Works well with Ubuntu 22.04 + Gnome + Wayland using a Sapphire Radeon Pulse RX 5600 XT which does PCIE 4.0 and has for a long time now.  The card actually handles it very easily at 120hz on gnome for daily grinds, fans are not even moving at the moment.  The booklet instructions are confusing, so while waiting for the monitor to ship I would suggest watching some unboxing.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 34-Inch Odyssey G85SB Series QD-OLED Ultra WQHD Curved Gaming Monitor, 175Hz, 0.03ms, DisplayHDR True Black 400, AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, Advanced Game Streaming, LS34BG850SNXZA, 2023

text_fidelity_a:
VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube A warning to first time users, you may experience the microphone picking up background noise. It's very sensitive. Be prepared to set-up an area for recording if you are wanting to get clean audio. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came in a fairly plain box with a large hard foam protective insert. This microphone seems to be a great starting point for anyone interested in a higher quality microphone. I can whole heartedly recommend it.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone is a USB interface microphone that is a large step-up in quality to those used to the basic microphones that come with many web cameras. It provides a higher sensitivity to sounds; enabling both a greater ability to pick up lower volume noises and the ability to comprehend higher volume ones.

The lower volumes it was able to obtain included whispering, including the mouth noises associated with ASMR videos, and keystrokes from a non-mechanical keyboard roughly 6 feet away [With it's recording volume turned down to 50%]. On the higher end of volume it is able to accommodate singing, yelling, and screaming; by not topping out what it able to accommodate this allowed for wide arrays of vocals and would assist with those wanting to record instruments. I did many different experiments to test the range at home on different days.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came with a short stand and pop filter that is attached to the stand by goose neck. The stand and metallic goose neck are both adjustable to assist with angling, but it is not vertically adjustable. The microphone, when pointing directly up, is about 26 cm / 10 in in height to the top of the microphone. It has a rubber ball footed desktop tripod for stability. The microphone can also detach from the included stand and be mounted to a standard size tripod or any other compatible stand, making the pop filter necessary depending on setup.

I had a great experience using VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone to audition for a voice acting role organized by fellow fans of an animated series. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone certainly made me sound much better than my webcam microphone is able to do. I have been using this for cooperative game-play online as well. This is a great value, especially at the price point.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it informative and helpful.
text_fidelity_b: VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube

text_fidelity_a:
Sony Cyber-shot DSC-H55 14.1MP Digital Camera with 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom with SteadyShot Image Stabilization and 3.0 inch LCD (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Sony Cyber-shot DSC -H 55.
I have owned two other cameras in the past. My last Camera, before this one, was a 12 Megapixel. And I thought it, at first to be ALL THAT. This was only because my previous camera had been a four Megapixel. I was so impressed with the increase in the resolution that is all I could see was the ability to crop photos to a better end then I had been able to. After the newness had worn off I began to realize the Cameron was just a lemon. So with this camera, that mistake will not happen again. The (14 Megapixel) of this Sony camera is not that different from my (12 Megapixel) camera that I am replacing. So I will look past the resolution difference with ease.
However the (10 x) zoom lens is NEW. Not only to me, but to all (point and shoot) cameras I have ever seen. Now, the 10 x zoom lens that I am talking about is NOT digital zoom. But rather, purely optical. There is a digital zoom offered in the menus of this camera. But I simply turned this feature off. If I want to do any digital zoom, I'll do it in Photoshop on my own time.
Other perks include; a battery and charger. The battery is lithium. And knowing that a lithium battery must be conditioned before its true capacity can ever be obtained. And even before the battery had been `conditioned' it was still able to take approximately 400 shots. And of course four or five HRS of me playing around in the menus with the features. And I know from past experience this can be one of the biggest power drains on a camera battery. And this is only the first cycle. I don't foresee a need in my future to buy a spear battery.
While I am on the subject of batteries, I need to mention. The battery charger is a cute little thing. The part of the plug that actually goes into the wall will fold into the plastic housing. So it is not a burdensome piece of machinery to store. And the whole thing is extremely small. It is only 3"x2"x1". To me that sounds ridiculously small, and if it were not right here in front of me I might not even believe. But it is true. It will fit in my small camera case, instead of the drawer. I already have enough mess around my room.
Also about batteries, there is a handy little gauge, on the LCD screen, that reports the amount of battery left by a four bar indicator (like a cell phone).
I spoke earlier about the massive zoom lens. But I didn't even tell how this camera can also take a macro picture up to about 8" away at full wide angle (zoom out). The 8" I just spoke could be off a little by + or - an inch. The manual that could tell me for sure is over there in that box, and I am over here. And I'm a lazy person.
I'm really impressed at how small this camera is. It will fit very nicely, with lots of room to spare, in my chest pocket. I do wear a 2X shirt, but there is so much room left over, I bet you could fit this camera in a large size pocket. I haven't had a chance to test it; I'm just using my best estimate. On outings, being able to tuck this camera away in my pocket will be way awesome. And it is so light weight.
And it weighs very, very little for such a nice camera. I have a cordless optical mouse hooked up to this computer. So by comparing weight, the mouse is the more heavy of the two.
I think I have touched on the biggest topics I can think of at this sitting, but to sum this up. This is the best camera I (personally) have ever owned. This would include 2 other digital cameras (one SLR type & one point and shoot) and a couple `film cameras' 110 and a 35mm SLR my uncle left to me. And after comparing it with all the other ones available at the stores, it IS the best. I compare every time a store has a display, to see if mine is still better. Even some of the `better' SLR types that sell for $100's, fall short. I would be really upset to see that a little `point & shoot' can beat my $800 `SLR type' camera.
At $225 and $25 3 year extended warranty from Samsclub, I have a new gizmo and I did not break the bank.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-H55 14.1MP Digital Camera with 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom with SteadyShot Image Stabilization and 3.0 inch LCD (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

NETGEAR 16-Port Gigabit Ethernet Unmanaged Switch (GS116NA) - Desktop or Wall Mount, and Limited Lifetime Protection I own 2 of these 16 port switches housed in a wiring cabinet in a closet and another, a [[ASIN:B00MPVR50A NETGEAR 8-Port Gigabit Switch (GS108)]] at my computer desk mounted to the wall, and an, [[ASIN:B00MPVR50A NETGEAR 8-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch (GS108)]] behind the LR TV, then another 3 separate bedroom TV's (kids and my br) have [[ASIN:B002NVOLGI Netgear GS605 5-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch]] behind them for all the various game systems, video devices etc. I purchased them to upgrade my network from older legacy 10/100 switches a few years back. I am very easily able to maintain, GB transfer levels, and all devices on my network are able to pull great speed tests.

I used the switches to segment my network into logical groups, the cabinet, holds the main switch's that run to things like the modem, router, alarm panel, other WiFi AP's, and they connect to my other switches.

One pro tip if you have young kids in the home, make sure and keep the network switches where they (young kids) cannot plug cords into it. At the time my 4 or 5 year old decided he would help dad by plugging the loose end of a cat5 cable into a spare port on the switch. You can guess it wreaked havoc on my system causing crashes etc.

These have held up well to years of use and show no signs of letting me down. I will certainly buy NETGEAR again.

text_fidelity_a: Polaroid Originals OneStep 2 VF - Summer Blue (9016) My youngest son graduated from high school this past weekend. I wanted him to be able to capture memories. Kids today use their cameras, but never go on to print out the photos. Of course, I am from a generation where we use to print out photos and scrapbook or place them in a photobook. Instead kids today Instagram or Snapchat, simply posting a memory that will be gone if those platforms crash. So, I instead am trying to get my son to capture some moments on film. The Polaroid Original One Step 2 provided gives him that option. Simply point and shoot. Instant fun, instant prints, instant memories captured.  I remember begging for a Polaroid when I was younger.  My parents said that they were expensive, and it seemed to take some time before “Santa” gave me one. But once I did, I enjoyed snapping photos and waiting those few minutes until the photo came to life before my eyes. So really, this is more nostalgic than practical. I wanted my son to know the wonder of a Polaroid. So of course, this review is from that prospective. The One Step 2 is easy to load. There is a built-in flash and other great features. Unlike the old Polaroids, this one has a built-in rechargeable battery. That’s a very nice feature. The only thing is that this camera DOES NOT come with film, but that was pretty easy to rectify. I simply ordered mine on Amazon. While some would say that the film is kind of expensive, 8 pics for about $18.00 which equals a little over $2 a photo, it is FUN and the exciting thing is now you can get black & white film. How much fun is that? Start capturing your memories. 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Originals OneStep 2 VF - Summer Blue (9016)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech 910-000253 VX Nano Cordless Laser Mouse Retail Logitech says that their products are designed to move you, and this mouse sure lives up to that promise. Seconds after opening the beautifully packaged box, I was up and running and you can do it too. The instructions tell you everything you need to know, from how to put in the batteries (2 x AAA, included), how to turn it on (power button on the bottom), and where to insert the Nano receiver (USB port). For more features, Windows users can install the software included, and Mac users can go get the download.

Installation takes quite a few minutes, but once that's over, your mouse gets super powers, and can scroll from side to side (perfect for those extra wide pages), help you search the internet with the push of a button, and also navigate backwards and forwards between internet pages. How cool is that?

Here's all the OTHER good stuff about the VX Nano:

1. It's cordless
2. It's compact and cute, and oh so ergonomic (at least for small hands)
3. The MicroGear Precision Scroll Wheel (fancy name for the wheel thing between the buttons that you scroll with) has two modes: Hyper-Fast, for when you need to scroll down long documents at warp speed, and Ratchet, for when you don't have a long, long way to run. You switch between them by simply pressing down on the wheel. (Tilting the same wheel left or right gives you the side by side scrolling once you've installed the software)
4. There's a LED light to tell you when your batteries need changing
5. There's a compartment at the bottom of the mouse to store the Nano-receiver securely. Alternately, you can just leave the little thing attached to your notebook USB port.
6. The package includes a nice Logitech zippered case to keep your mouse snug as a bug in a rug.
7. You can use it on your desktop machine too. It comes with an "extension cord" that you plug into the USB port of your CPU, and insert the Nano-receiver into the little gizmo at the other end, and you're all set. I didn't even have to evict the regular mouse that was already living on my mouse pad.

Believe me, after you've gone Nano you'll never want to go back to cords again.

I Like To Move It Move It
I Like To Move It Move It
I Like To Move It Move It
You'll Like To (MOVE IT!)

Amanda Richards, September 30, 2007

Arkon Robust Headrest Tablet Mount for iPad Air 2 iPad Pro iPad Retail Black The Arkon Tablet arm everything that you see in the pictures:
- Two clamps that secure tightly to the metal posts on a car's headrest.
- The arm is extendable and can be locked in to position.
- There are two sets of L brackets to allow for multiple configurations depending on the size of your tablet.
- The L brackets have rubber footing that securely hold the tablet.

My concerns:
- The screws that tighten the clamps to the headrest posts are very very thin. I can see them breaking if someone tightens them too much.
- The tablet mount is held to the extendable arm using a ball joint. While a ball joint works well for a cell phone, my concern is that tablets are much heavier and that the ball joint would slip -- especially with car vibrations. It is necessary to tighten the ball joint a lot in order for it to stay put.

I do not deduct any stars for these concerns because they have not happened to me, but potential design flaws should be pointed out.

For my iPad, I use two long and two short L brackets (exactly as you see in the sample picture). This is the perfect size for the ipad. The position that of the iPad at the center of the car means both kids are able to see the videos comfortably on long car trips.

Conversely: 1 = much worse than expected. 2 = worse than expected. This New Stars Scale thus allows a negative rating as some have complained that they "Can't give negative 5 stars." Well now you can as 1 and 2 are in effect negative ratings, being lower than 3 which is essentially "OK. It works as expected, no better, no worse."

Well this mouse gets a New Stars Scale rating of only 2 because there is no way by glancing at it to tell if it is on or off. Rather one has to either 1) wiggle the mouse and see on the computer screen - if it is up and running - what the cursor does, or even if it is there or 2) pick up the mouse and look at the tiny black on/off switch on the bottom. Whether on or off, the tracking beam is invisible to the human eye.

Whereas my Amazon Basics mouse has a red jewel on top that lights up when it is on. Good idea! And it has a solid feel and better click. It is better then expected (or normal) so it gets a 4.

So I won't be buying the Logitech M170 mouse again.

text_fidelity_a:
VideoSecu Low Profile TV Wall Mount Bracket for Most 32" - 75" LCD LED UHD Plasma HDTV, Compatible with Sony Bravia Samsung LG Haier Vizio Sharp AQUOS Westinghouse Pioneer ProScan Toshiba 1NN The bracket is incredible! I used it on a Samsung Plasma 60 inch ,(600x400-Vesa) PN60F5500. At first I was a little wary. The plasma is 2013 model ,weighs by itself about 60 pounds.Its solid, and the weight of my TV held it down without using security brackets. You need at least an 18 inch long screw driver because you cannot reach behind it once installed. A few turns and you're set. I found it easier to unscrew , first tighten , then go in the opposite direction so it locks the screwdriver in the center making it easier to remove. I left it untighten, since it held in place without them.

Im not a professional installer (like drilling holes and finding a stud in the wall) but was able to use my old screws from the wall to install this mount from my older plasma.. I did however have to drill 2 more at the bottom because of the Vesa difference. Beyond that, everything else was simple.Its solid once installed, very easy, and simple to understand.

CON: Personal pet peeve. The only con is on 60 inch TVs you cannot reach behind easily to use the security brackets.You have to use an 18 inch long screw driver or similar size to tighten them. (booklet does not say this . Only says use a screwdriver)They are not needed because the weight of the TV holds in in place. In my opinion, I like to do everything by the instructions. Not tighten the security brackets made me feel like I skipped a step. I will say its stays in place, and does not move, jiggle etc. Lifting the bottom of a 60 inch is not easy, so there is no worry about it being easily done, even by a kid since the hooks are on the top. Other reviewers have said security brackets are not needed to hold it in place. I just left them barely connected so I could have the option to screw on later.

PS: If you own a 60 inch and im guessing 65 (max size), it will not look like the picture after adding the back portions on the TV. At first I was under the impression it would not work, but adjusted the height on the TV brackets and it fit barely, but did fit.It does work on a (600x400) vesa mount TV.
text_fidelity_b: VideoSecu Low Profile TV Wall Mount Bracket for Most 32" - 75" LCD LED UHD Plasma HDTV, Compatible with Sony Bravia Samsung LG Haier Vizio Sharp AQUOS Westinghouse Pioneer ProScan Toshiba 1NN

LENRUE Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built-in-Mic,Handsfree Call,AUX Line,TF Card for iPhone Ipad Android Smartphone and More (Grey) I've been wanting my own bluetooth speaker forever. The interesting thing is that I'm not even interested in the bluetooth capability. I want the aux connection for my first generation iPod, which doesn't have bluetooth technology. My iPhone just doesn't have the space for all the music I have on the iPod, plus I don't want to use up data streaming Pandora. Additionally, bluetooth and getting stuff to connect is just a pain. So, I've never tried to connect via bluetooth only the aux.

At first I thought I had dud. I charged it and went to push the power button and nothing happened. I read the tiny print in the instructions and still nothing. So, I went on YouTube to see if anyone made video about using this and of course there is! So, you have to press the power button until the device glows blue and beeps! No where on the instructions does it say to do this! So, once you do this, then you can follow the directions to use the speaker. If you are going to just use the aux plug then push the "M" button, which I think stands for mode. You're good to go.

Now this is tiny, so you're going to get a lot of output, but it what it does put out is a decent sound. I have used mine in a small pavilion for a party and on my front porch. At the party depending on the song, a few downloaded from the early aughts were too quiet to hear, but songs downloaded from iTunes or from CDs came out loud enough to hear throughout the pavilion. Just make sure the volume is up on your speaker AND your device. I've used for about 12 hours total. 4 hours here, 4 hours there, etc., and I still haven't charged it. So it holds a good charge to last through a party or an afternoon lounging on the porch.

You get an aux cord and a USB charging cord. So you can charge it on the computer or with a charger plug that uses a USB plug. The light ring turns red when charging and goes off when it's fully charged. The ring glows blue when it is on. It flashes when it it searching or looking for a bluetooth device. I bought this after a family member refused to let me use his "expensive someone is going to steal it" bluetooth speaker even though he never uses it (and I'm never in a situation to have someone steal it.)
text_fidelity_b: LENRUE Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built-in-Mic,Handsfree Call,AUX Line,TF Card for iPhone Ipad Android Smartphone and More (Grey)

eufy Security Indoor Cam E220, Pan & Tilt, Indoor Security Camera, 2K - 3 MP Wi-Fi Plug-in, Voice Assistant Compatibility, Night Vision, Motion Tracking, HomeBase 3 Compatible, Motion Only Alert Purchased two of these Eufy 2K cams to test out and determine if they're good enough to replace the Wyze cams. These Eufy cams definitely capture higher resolution, more detailed videos compared to the Wyze cam v2. The pan and tilt feature is great when I want to remotely check different parts of an area and the pan/tilt action is very silent. You can set the cam to automatically track/follow motion when it's detected. The amount of time it takes to go to live view on a cam is within a couple of seconds and the alerts for motion is definitely faster than the Wyze cam v2. The time from me waving my hand in front of the cam and getting an alert on my phone is about 3 seconds or less.

I did experience issues with one Eufy cam where it would randomly start panning by itself and would do a 360 degree pan. The Eufy app works overall, but I did notice several times I had connection issues when trying to live view, but this issue also happens on Wyze cams, too.

You can set the Eufy cam to record only when motion or sound is detected or set the cam to continuous recording. If you choose continuous recording the video resolution will be reduced to 1080p resolution. For motion recording you can set up activity zones (specific areas you want to detect motion), adjust motion detection sensitivity, detect people, detect pets, and detect all other motion. Eufy's app is still missing the ability to view multiple live views of cams at the same time, which is a shame and hopefully they have a software update for that.

Overall, the Eufy 2k cam has great video quality, the pan/tilt motion is useful and silent, has a lot of features, and the price is competitive. They go on sale from time to time, so if you're not in a hurry then I'd wait for a sale.
text_fidelity_b: eufy Security Indoor Cam E220, Pan & Tilt, Indoor Security Camera, 2K - 3 MP Wi-Fi Plug-in, Voice Assistant Compatibility, Night Vision, Motion Tracking, HomeBase 3 Compatible, Motion Only Alert

Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) I've been using a Keurig machine for several years -- I currently own 2 of them. But I've always had an ethical issue with all the little plastic cups that get tossed into the environment. To that end, I've tried and used several different varieties of reusable K-cups, and had finally settled on the Ekobrew cups.

I was offered an opportunity to try this set, and decided to do a side-by-side comparison. The results were interesting. These Brewooze cups perform just as good as the more expensive Ekobrew cups.

I tried several different coffees and several different grinds. As with all reusable cups, you have to be careful how fine/coarse the grind is. Too coarse, and you get weaker coffee; too fine, and you get either overflow and/or sludge. I found that a medium-fine grind worked best for both cup brands. This way, I get the right strength and almost no powdery sludge in the bottom of the cup. One advantage of the Brewooze over the Ekobrew: I was able to use LESS coffee in the cup to get the right brew strength. With the Ekobrew, I needed to fill the cup; with the Brewooze, I filled it about 2/3 full to get the same flavor/strength.

As with all reusable K-cups, you need to take care when you seal them prior to use. These are no trouble to seal correctly -- you can easily see if there are gaps and do an extra "squeeze." Inserting them into the machine takes a bit of attention, too -- otherwise, you can pierce the cup. There are arrows on the lid that show which direction, so that shouldn't be a problem.

This set comes with 20 paper filters plus a replacement charcoal filter for the Keurig filter wand. I didn't see much advantage to the paper filters except possibly ease of cleaning. The coffee was weaker, and using a finer grind didn't seem to help. And it still resulted in some grinds getting "around" the paper filter and onto the mesh, so I still had to clean the cup. It's not a big deal, really -- the cups are easy to rinse clean after use. So I won't be using the paper filters, but you may find them useful.

I'm a little surprised at how nicely these performed, given the price. You get 3 cups (brown, medium tan, and light tan color -- the photo makes them look orange, but they're more of a tan/brown), so if you want to assign a color to different family members, there you go. Since I usually brew 2 cups into a large mug, I just fill 2 of them with the same coffee and run them one after the other in the morning.

kI have to say I was impressed. I didn't expect these to perform as well as they did. Definitely comparable to the Ek​​​​obrew so far -- the only question I have is durability, and only time will tell. I've been using these for about 4 days, and after the initial side-by-side test (when I brewed about 12 cups total), I've been brewing 2-3 cups every morning, rotating them, cleaning after each use, and so far, no signs of any wear problems. If I notice a serious issue, I'll update this review.

SUDOKEJI 1000W Pure Sine Wave Inverter Power Inverter Peak Power 2000W 12V DC to 110V 120V AC with LED Display 3 AC Outlets & USB Port for RV Truck Boat This worked just fine for powering a few small items. When choosing what you are going to run on this add up the total wattage of all devices, then add at least 50% more to account for peaks or spikes in the power draw. For example if your coffee maker draws 500 watts, your laptop 300 watts, and your toaster 200 watts (total, 1000 watts) you should account for the extra 50% (1000watts + 500 watts (the 50%)=1500watts). In this example, a minimum 1500 watt inverter should be used.

If the item is motor driven, it requires additional start-up (surge) wattage (typically 2-3 times the continuous wattage required) to start the device. For example, a miter saw that runs at 700 watts might require 1400 watts to start up. If your inverter only supplies 1000 watts, you will not be able to start it up. In this case, you would want to select an inverter rated at least 1400 surge watts to handle start-up needs.

I understand how wattage works and for someone who doesn't, any inverter could fail if overloaded with more power than it can handle. An overload feature that automatically shuts the device off would be helpful for anyone who is unsure. This has an overload feature, but if you blow a fuse, you'll have to replace it. Do your research and know how this works, and it'll work fine.
text_fidelity_b: SUDOKEJI 1000W Pure Sine Wave Inverter Power Inverter Peak Power 2000W 12V DC to 110V 120V AC with LED Display 3 AC Outlets & USB Port for RV Truck Boat

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin vívofit 2 Activity Tracker, White The circumference of my wrist is 5 1/4 inches above the bone which is fairly small and the small wristband fits perfectly, there are still 5 holes (1.5 inches) left to make it smaller.

The two reasons I went for this activity tracker are it is waterproof and the battery lasts one year... for me these are the most important reasons because I really hate all this constant charging of gadgets.

Syncing is easy, at the end of the day I just press one button and it syncs with my smartphone, it also comes with a little blue-tooth USB attachment if you want to sync it with your computer. I've read they will add autosync with the next software update which is supposed to arrive shortly.

You get to choose what to see on your screen when you press the button, I went with steps, goal, distance and time. You can also add the date, calories and heart rate if you are wearing a strap.

I absolutely love how it feels, it doesn't bother me at all, you don't have to wear it real tight and the silicon is very soft.

The reason I took one star off is that the beep sound which comes on after one hour of inactivity (when the red warning line appears) is way, way, way too quiet. I set an alarm just to check on the beep sound and it was so short and subtle, if there would be any kind of background noise you won't be able to hear it at all.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin vívofit 2 Activity Tracker, White

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba Canvio Basics 1TB Portable Hard Drive - Black (HDTB310XK3AA) PERFECT!

I was looking for a MAC time machine backup drive and noticed the external drives labeled as MAC were $10 - $15 more. I then read the Q&A on this drive and someone gave the most perfect instructions:

"right out of the box it's not Mac ready, but the solution is real easy. You go to Utilities and open up Disk Utility. With the drive plugged in, select it and go to the Erase tab and there should be a drop down menu with Format. Select Mac OS and click erase and after that's done, the drive should be formatted for Mac and you can save to your heart's content."

I might only add where to find Disk Utility in case you didn't know ... in finder go to the applications folder and in that folder is utilities and in that folder is disk utility.

I did just as the person in Q&A said and the second it was done reformatting a box came up asking if I wanted to use this drive as a time machine backup drive. I said yes, and within 107 seconds I was done. Color me impressed!

We got the 1tb drive because we have a 1tb 21.5" iMac from Nov 2013.

I hope this helps someone. I will update this review later as to longevity of the drive.

UPDATE: May 6, 2018
7 months later and this little backup drive does what it should do. We have never needed to utilize the files it stores, but it is nice to know the files are there. I periodically check to make sure my Mac is recording on this drive and it functions perfectly as a time machine drive.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba Canvio Basics 1TB Portable Hard Drive - Black (HDTB310XK3AA)

text_fidelity_a:
Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black) Once calibrated, this PC tablet works wonderfully. It is responsive to the stowable stylus or a tap of my fingernail, and I can even scroll with my thumb after adjusting the right edge width. The screen is sharp and clear, and it's speedy enough for pleasurable surfing and blog-reading, which is what I mostly want to use it for. I have not watched any HD movies on it yet, although the sample movie clip included with the computer shows what it's capable of...and it's gorgeous.

But I have a problem with the Archos 9. Because there is no fan, which makes for a very quiet experience, the lithium battery does get hot when held in your hands. Now, maybe there are people who will use this computer by pulling out the little easel-like stick in the back, but not me. I want to curl up on the sofa with it like a book. So I could see immediately that I wanted to rotate my Archos 9 PC Tablet's screen to portrait orientation so the battery would be at the top and not bother me so much. Well, doing so was a BIG mistake. Once you rotate the screen, it's pretty much impossible to recalibrate it; trying to move the cursor is like trying to walk without an inner ear: Directions ceased to make sense and I'd skew off East (or was it West?) when I meant to move North. It was all I could do to manage to restore the computer to its earlier state.

The little end piece of the easel-like appendage pulled off and I had to super-glue it back on, but that wasn't such a big deal. This appendage also stows into the back of the computer, and it can be pulled out short or long depending on whether you are watching a movie or trying to type on the on-screen keyboard. I can see it for watching a movie, but there's no way I'd ever try to type on the on-screen keyboard. Hunt-and-peck with the stylus is quicker. Needless to say, I will reach for my laptop if I have to do much typing.

I installed Skype, but it was too slow to show video unless I stopped everything else from running. This is fine with me, however, because I prefer to use Skype without the visuals. Google Chrome runs very well on it. I found I preferred the software keyboard (which you can drag around the screen) to the one that pops up when you press the keyboard key. I found that by keeping the former loaded and minimized to the tray, I can get around and do things online pretty efficiently. I just wish that battery didn't get so hot OR that I could easily/reliably rotate the screen to portrait. I gave this computer four stars because, on the whole, it's quite nice. But I must say that I am not likely to reach for the Archos 9 very often because of the discomfort from the battery heat when holding it in my hands. If they will come out with a software upgrade that will make screen rotation practical, then I will be a lot happier with this tablet PC.

A word to the wise: Immediately when you take your Archos 9 out of the box and get the software installed, you need to back it up. Don't wait a second longer than you have to. I was able to restore mine to its pristine newly installed state, but had I not backed it up, the whole thing would have been trashed by my little screen rotation exploit. You don't have a restore disk with this product. So be careful.
text_fidelity_b: Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
BOSS Audio Systems B9351WRC Double Din, Touchscreen, Bluetooth, DVD CD MP3 USB SD AM FM Car Stereo, 6.2 Inch Digital LCD Monitor, Wireless Remote, Wireless Rear License Plate Camera. I knew, due to my disability, that I was going to need to find a professional installer to install this Boss Audio Systems B9351WRC head unit and wireless reverse camera along with two replacement door speakers I decided needed replacement (and wow, they really needed replacing). The installation took approximately three hours or so. The only problem which may not be a problem but I'm a worrier. The bracket for the wireless reverse camera somewhat, but not entirely, covers the plate expiration stickers somewhat. Other than that the head unit fit as good if not better than the stock radio fit. in the dashboard.
This radio plays AM/FM stations though there's very few decent radio stations around here. The unit also plays from USB thumb drives which plugs into a port under a panel under the volume/pause/power button. I put 600+ songs on a USB 2.0 16 GB driver and it played everything as far as I could tell. There might be a couple VBR or odd format MP3 files it may not play but I haven't gotten to them yes. Nothing's refused to play and even a couple that had imbedded album artwork actually showed up but so small it was almost impossible to see and I had no idea how to make it better. The instructions in the manual were basically "Play with things and see what happens!" more than specific directions how different functions work.
What I went with, is a 32 gig micro-SD card that had the same 600+ songs the thumb drive has. But with the micro-SD card you can close the hatch under the volume and control knob which you couldn't with the thumb drive. There's also an AUX input jack for old style MP3 players and phones.
The six inch screen is sharp and crisp. The backup camera, even with a streetlight thirty feet away had more than enough light to back out of my garage. I even backed down the street a ways in almost complete darkness and could see just fine with just the reverse lights on the car. Now as long as no cops have a problem with it I'm golden.
I tried home burned CDs and while it took a few seconds longer to recognize it played them fine. I tried store bought CDs and they played right off the bat. OH! and it plays DVD discs jut fine in case my passenger wants to watch a movie as we drive. I promise I'm no dumb enough to watch a movie while I drive.
According to the installer I can leave the micro SD card in the unit all the time. So, 600+ songs anytime I want which I can shuffle or randomly pick and play songs anytime I want. I couldn't be happier. With the stock deck I'd sometimes get to my destination just as the deck decided to recognize the CD so this deck is a godsend when I really needed a new one. Now with as many songs as I can cram into a 32 gig drive. Right now I've got 687 songs and tons of free space. I may have to start buying more music and ripping some more albums from my collection to add to my micro-SD card.
So I can play hundreds, thousands of MP3 songs on a micro-SD card. I can play CDs both homemade and store bought. I can watch DVDs on a pretty sharp (all settings can be changed in the system) the dimmer is a bit bright until it goes off completely but it's not too bad or too bright. There's a user setting EQ option as well as several other preset settings to choose from. There are options to add sound effects such as large hall, church, cavern, etc. I avoided them entirely and set my own EQ settings with the loudness off. The new speakers sound great for high end and midrange. The stock back speakers add some needed bass.
All in all? This is an affordable head unit with all the features and functions one could ask for. It comes with a remote that I'm not sure I'm even going to keep anywhere in the car. Anything you need to do can be done on the deck and no one's sitting in the back seat of a '07 Hyundai Accent, seriously. So the remote is useless but amusing.
I love this unit, the backup cam is awesome, The many ways to play music. The fit and finish, it's close to perfect.
This a little long and meandering review but I really like this radio and I'm glad I replaced the door speakers and went with a professional installer who's basically given me a lifetime warranty on his labor. I couldn't be happier.

Update 04-04-2017: It's been nearly six months since I had this head unit and backup camera installed. Radio reception is still bad, I still despise listening to radio so that's no big deal. Have kept a micro SD card loaded with hundreds of songs installed. Turn the unit on it automatically defaults to that. Everything is still working fine. Professional installation was worth the money.
text_fidelity_b: BOSS Audio Systems B9351WRC Double Din, Touchscreen, Bluetooth, DVD CD MP3 USB SD AM FM Car Stereo, 6.2 Inch Digital LCD Monitor, Wireless Remote, Wireless Rear License Plate Camera.

text_fidelity_a: FRAMEO 10.1 Inch Smart WiFi Digital Photo Frame 1280x800 IPS LCD Touch Screen, Auto-Rotate Portrait and Landscape, Built in 16GB Memory, Share Moments Instantly via Frameo App from Anywhere I ❤️ my Frameo!! I initially bought one for my Dad and he loved it so much, I decided to get one for my family. It is SO MUCH FUN! And an excellent solution to “what should I do with all the pictures on my phone’s camera roll?” There isn’t really any assembly. You’ll need to install the frameo app and create an account. Frameo will hold all your photos for a lifetime too. From the app, you can select any photo off your camera roll and with a few taps, send it to your frame. You can label each pix if desired. Frameo also allows me to share my frame, via a numerical code, to anyone else after they download the app. So, my daughter at college can send pix to my frame and I can see them in seconds. The frame holds like, 20,000 photos. Each one is posted for about 20 seconds. You can easily tap and drag to scroll forwards or backwards on the frame. You also don’t need wifi to SEE pictures. You need wifi to UPLOAD additional pictures and for others to share the frame. In theory, you could set this up with your personal wifi, load it with as many pictures as you want, then have your elderly parent simply plug it in at their house. It will scroll through all the photos you loaded. You just can’t add more until it’s connected to wifi. It’s a special gift and it’s been fun for personal use too. I highly recommend!

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball Mouse with Touch Scroll Ring (K72352US),Black If you want the trackball for gaming or general PC getting around. The choices I see, are getting worse. I first got hooked on the wired Logitech Marble. Loved and still own a few. Now, I needed a wireless option and tried one from Logitech and a few other brands. Just have trouble getting used to the side marble and it wasn't great for gaming and the others were cheap and felt low quality.

Brings us to the Kensington Orbit. For me, it is as close to the Marble as I have found so far in a wireless version. Good range and plenty response options. Ball is in the center where I prefer to have it. 2 buttons the way a mouse was meant to be (although a couple tiny programable buttons would be nice at this price). Yet not all is perfect, but I am coping with it. The tricky bit for me that hinders a higher rating. First, the right click button is too big. There is no where for my pinky finger to rest without clicking. Please revise the design just a bit for the base to ride a bit higher or the button to get a bit smaller. Or add a flip up piece to partially cover the button to prevent pushing it (likely to 3D print something for my use). Who needs the right click button to be so prominent. Secondly, It might be me, but the sliders/scroll on either side of the ball are not great. They hesitate and don't react to my touch too well, but it might be me with rough fingers.

I will keep the mouse because it works well for what I need right now. But, Hey Kensington, consider a revised model that has room for the finger to rest somewhere on the right that does no result in a button press. Can't be the only one. Or maybe that is a different model you already sell? My choices were limited when I ordered.
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball Mouse with Touch Scroll Ring (K72352US),Black

iPad Pro 10.5 Case with Wireless Keyboard, Janvvoo Ultra-Thin Lightweight Bluetooth Keyboard with Magnetically Intelligent Switch and Multi-Angle Stand for Apple iPad Pro 10.5 inch Tablet I have owned this shredder for over six years, and it has endured some heavy use. It is the second home-shredder I've owned, and it is much the better of the two. It is heavy enough that it doesn't tip over, but not so heavy it can't be hauled from room to room by someone moderately strong. The front compartment holding the shredded paper is easily removed--in an identical fashion to our dehumidifier's bucket. You pull on it and the bucket comes out with a forward motion. The sound the shredder makes when in action is loud, as one would expect, but not so loud that you need protective ear plugs, such as for when you are near a kitchen blender, blow dryer, leaf blower or lawn mower.

The main thing to be careful about is to not get impatient and overload the shredder blades. Yes, you can use the backup function to try and back out paper you have overloaded it with, but it is a pain. Secondly, be sure and feed paper in straight. If you feed it in crooked, that, too, is a prescription for a jam.

When I am shredding, I lay down either a bed sheet or a tarp and set the shredder in the middle of it. This helps me corral the scraps of shredded paper flying around when I empty the bucket into a trash bag. Another option is to shred in your garage or basement, if you have such spaces, and use a [[ASIN:B00005AXI1 Shop-Vac]] to clean up afterwards. If you do it inside your house, plan on having to use a regular vacuum to clean up after each use, because a mess is almost unavoidable no matter how careful you are since this shredder is turning private papers into confetti. That's great for the shredder's intended purpose, but it does have a tendency to give whatever room you are using a strong resemblance to Times Square on New Year's Eve.
text_fidelity_b: iPad Pro 10.5 Case with Wireless Keyboard, Janvvoo Ultra-Thin Lightweight Bluetooth Keyboard with Magnetically Intelligent Switch and Multi-Angle Stand for Apple iPad Pro 10.5 inch Tablet

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech for Creators Blue Yeti X Professional USB Condenser Microphone for PC, Mac,Gaming,Recording, Streaming, Podcasting on PC, Desktop Mic High-Res Metering, LED Lighting,Blue VO!CE Effects-Black This is a fancier version of the popular Blue Yeti amateur-quality USB microphone with a much higher price tag ($170 vs $110). For the extra money, you get 4 condensers (instead of 3) to give you higher-resolution 24-bit audio (instead of 16-bit) plus a bunch of fancier control and display options. The new microphone has the same directional recording patterns to isolate the recording to your intended audio sources. Is the new microphone worth the extra money? If you really need 24-bit audio, then definitely yes. If not, the new display and control features are more convenient than a huge jump in functionality. The Blue Yeti is still a great microphone for amateur USB recording (podcasts, musical performances, etc). The new version is a step forward, but not worth the price for everyone.

My biggest complaint is that the new microphone uses the same ancient mini-USB interface as the old one. Modern ultralight laptops are moving to the USB-C standard and mini-USB is 2 generations old. You could use a USB-C hub to give you a mini-USB interface, but I wish all modern devices came with USB-C ports since this has been the standard for the last few years.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech for Creators Blue Yeti X Professional USB Condenser Microphone for PC, Mac,Gaming,Recording, Streaming, Podcasting on PC, Desktop Mic High-Res Metering, LED Lighting,Blue VO!CE Effects-Black

They sound great compared to a pair of Skullcandy Crusher's headphones  retail price $99 that I formally owned. These cost me one quarter of the price and sound just as good. The driver on these headsets do not need a bass boost battery like the Crusher's optimally provided,  the bass sounds awesome just on their own because the size of the driver is sufficient. These are comfortable enough on your ears to to ware them for about 2 to 3 hours at that time you may consider a break. This is is when you start to feel fatigue. I've used many headsets before, gaming headsets or general music headsets and I was surprised by the sound. You will need an inline microphone if you want to use them in a wired fashion. These are compatible with inline mics I tried them. For $10 you can get an inline mic, at that point they also become gaming headsets and will work with video game consoles. Although they have a mic built in when using them wireless they  will require an inline mic if you want to use them while taking a call when plugged in.

And while this unit may not protect your devices from a direct lighting strike it will definitely protect from fluctuations in current.

This 6 outlet, 2 USB surge protector is easily mountable using the 2 included screws. I simply placed the bottom on my printer / scanner and hit copy - that provides an exact mounting template. Following that, tape the piece of paper where you want to mount, pre drill small pilot holes through the paper marking where your screws go, remove paper, insert screws, mount.

The 2 USB (2.4A each) easily accommodates most USB plugs and self regulates charging speed to charge your devices at the fastest possible speed.

There are 6 surge protected, 3 prong outlets. The farthest one to the right is offset to provide room for larger brick style plugs.

I mounted mine to the underside of my laptop desk next to the couch and it has operated perfectly.

While the box shows that the power button illuminates a blue color when on, it does not. I checked with the manufacturer and that is not a defect - there is no LED light there. Not a big deal.

This would be the perfect surge protector / outlet strip for next to the bed, taking on cruises or other locations where you need extra outlets and protection from electrical fluctuations.

Divoom Pixoo-64 - WiFi Pixel Cloud Digital Frame with APP Control,64 X 64 LED Panel Display Frame for Gaming Room Decoration/Social Media Fans Counter THE GOOD:
--------------
* High quality, and very professionally manufactured.
* At it's most basic function, it is simply an animated picture frame, and the images are stylized to look pixelated.
* Downloading the app, Divoom, and setting things up was pretty self explanatory and intuitive.
* USB-C power port, which means no worries about which way the cable plugs in like the hassle of micro usb cables.
* Hang or use the included kick-stand.
* Overall, just something really fun to play with. A conversation piece for sure.

THE BAD:
------------
* Social media and game linking are very limited. My son would go bonkers if we can somehow link Roblox. There is Fortnite though. He doesn't play that as much, but we were able to link Fortnite, and it showed his stats.
* The screen doesn't really pop as much as I'd like. It's decent, but it would be nicer if it was brighter.
* It's covered by two film protections, full of bubbles. There should have been some easy lifting tabs. There are no lifting tabs, and the films run right up against the bezel. Making it extremely difficult to lift an edge. You feel like you're scratching the screen just trying to lift this film. I got the top film off. The second film was too difficult, so instead of lifting the second film, I just took a credit card and straighten out all the bubbles, and kept it as a screen protector.

Overall, I'll go 4-Stars for this nifty piece of tech.
text_fidelity_b: Divoom Pixoo-64 - WiFi Pixel Cloud Digital Frame with APP Control,64 X 64 LED Panel Display Frame for Gaming Room Decoration/Social Media Fans Counter

CHUWI Hi8 8 inch Windows 10/Android 4.4 Dual Boot Tablet PC, with Features of Intel Quad Core, Full HD 19201200 IPS Screen, 2G RAM/32G ROM and Winkey Price is one thing that's good about this tablet. I have no problem with the cheap plastic all around (really, it almost felt like a disposable food tray), considering the price tag, but there were a couple of things I just couldn't get over.

- Whatever Android OS is installed here, it came without Google Play app. Once I installed it myself, it crashed every time I tried to download a new app from Google app store. This is unacceptable, especially considering that the tablet comes with almost no apps to begin with.
-By the time I updated Windows & set up tablet, it was already getting uncomfortable warm. I can't imagine what would happen if I tried doing something like taping a video for an hour.
- USB socket was loose, I had to jiggle the cable several times to get it charging, and a smallest shift caused it to disconnect again.
- I expected pretty poor camera from the specs, but this was outstanding. Video & images had all the charm and quality of those tiny snapshots from the early mobile phones. Made me kind of nostalgic, but I expect better from a current tablet.

Unrelatedly to the quality of tablet itself, I'm glad I got to try a Windows 10 OS tablet on a dual boot machine, so I know to avoid it from now on... a clumsy hybrid of desktop and tablet capabilities. Android booted and run reasonably fast, while Win 10 lagged on the same machine.

I'm returning it.

text_fidelity_a: Loutsbe Amplified Indoor HD Digital TV Antenna, Long 180 Miles Range,Support 4K 1080p and All Older TV's, Digital Antenna Amplifier Signal Booster-17ft Coax HDTV Cable,Freeview Life Local Channels Previously I had purchased a cheaper antenna that was not powered, as this one is.  It worked pretty well and got quite a few channels.  This one, however, works better and a few more channels come in clearly and consistently.  I tried it too without the USB power and it still works well, but without the power, not all the channels came in.  For the little extra that this costs over cheaper antennas, it is worth it.  The long cord on it is a wonderful plus, as you can position it quite a distance from the TV, unlike cheaper antennas that may have shorter cords.  The only thing I can see wrong with this is that since it is powered, it does use some electricity, whereas cheaper antennas don't.  Probably not really much electricity, but as we add more and more devices to our homes, those energy vampires can add up.  I suggest trying it with and without the power.  If you don't use the TV every day, unplug the power.  If you have pets that tend to chew things, watch out for them with the long cords on this.  Very satisfied with it and may get another one for other televisions in the house, once we cut off cable, which we are doing soon.  You recover your cost of the device with just one month of cable.  Extremely easy to install--under 5 minutes.

text_fidelity_a: DB Link RT4 4-Gauge Ring Terminal (2 Red and 2 Black) I received this order in a short time from placing the order.  The gold plated lugs are a good finish to make them look goldish, can't say if it is or not.  The inside diameter is 0.41 inch or 10.42mm.  The outside diameter of the Ring Terminal is 0.703in or 17.86mm.  The inside diameter of the cable lug hole is 0.331in. or 8.4mm and I noticed it does have a significant burr on the inside of the hole, thus reducing the inside diameter somewhat.  This burr when crimping will keep wire from being placed in the hole and bite the copper some during the crimp, abrading the wire. The slip-on insulation is easy to slide on and off the terminal so the cable should be easy to install. These terminals are good enough to make a proper cable end and I give them a four star rating for quality and pricing.
text_fidelity_b: DB Link RT4 4-Gauge Ring Terminal (2 Red and 2 Black)

Update July 2015, This TV has started acting up, I will be calling the 1-800-samsung and see what they say but with looking at the information on the web, it seems as if this tv is experiencing the same problems that their older TV's had which is power supply issues. It won't turn on sometimes, or it will take 30 seconds to power up, or other variations. I wish that I had known about these issues before I purchased this TV because I might have looked at different manufacturers..

Called the 800 number found out that manufacturer warranty is gone obviously. No offers of a free diagnostic or anything like that. They did provide a local number for technition but with it being a weekend chances are no one is there. I am going to see if there is anything I can visually pick up in the power supply and do some basic testing. (I did work as a power sports tech for a number of years and was a pretty serious computer hobbyist as well) after that will have to see. Will do another update after this is resolved one way or another

4K HDR HDMI Switch, Koopman 5 Ports 4K 60Hz HDMI 2.0 Switcher Selector with IR Remote, Supports Ultra HD Dolby Vision, High Speed (Max to 18.5Gbps), HDR10, HDCP 2.2 & 3D (I have received this product mostly free in exchange for an honest review)
I have been using a 3-in to 1-out HDMI switch for a couple years and recently the media box for one of my TVs died, so put on connected to the single HDMI input. It works just fine, but I have more than 3 devices I'd like to connect and reaching to change the input is annoying.
This has solved multiple problems. having 5 HDMI inputs is a pretty sweet deal. I've only tested 3 of them so far and they work just fine. One nice feature that I didn't expect is that it doesn't appear to let you switch to an input that doesn't have a device even powered on, at least using the remote.
The picture quality is just fine. I have nothing to compare it to, but it looks no worse than it ever did.
The nice feature of my previous switch was that it did not need to be powered. The Koopman one DOES need power. It comes with the micro USB cable and power adapter, but if your TV has an open 5v usb output, that might be more convenient. I had to plug it in. It's a minor annoyance, but if you're low on outlet space, keep it in mind.
It's small and light, so I'll need to anchor it in place so it's not flying off the stand. HDMI cables like to pull things awry. It's almost inconspicuous.
Speaking of HDMI cables, it doesn't come with one. I had expected (and didn't pay attention to the product description - so MY bad) at least a short one.
The remote is tiny. This is great because it doesn't take up much space, but I KNOW I'm going to spend a bunch of events looking for it in the couch or under the footrest or because a spider dragged it into their web in the corner. The remote worked from at least 15-20 feet away (as far as I could comfortably go), BUT, the angle of reception is not very wide. It might be about 60 degrees (I did not pull out the protractor). The box itself had a button on it, so if the remote goes temporarily missing, you can still tap your way between inputs.
I'll give it some time to see how it lasts. If it does well over time, I'll possibly buy another for another TV with only one HDMI input.
One cool improvement would be if it had an audio output, even in only a 1/8" port.
text_fidelity_b: 4K HDR HDMI Switch, Koopman 5 Ports 4K 60Hz HDMI 2.0 Switcher Selector with IR Remote, Supports Ultra HD Dolby Vision, High Speed (Max to 18.5Gbps), HDR10, HDCP 2.2 & 3D

Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black) Trying to decide if we were ready to cut the cord, we installed this antenna to see if we could get all the local channels. We got 40 digital channels about 20 miles west of Washington DC and the major networks are crystal clear.

The network towers we use are clustered together about 20 miles away. We have 2 or more topographical obstructions between our house and the towers (no line of sight). The Noise Margin on the networks is 35-40 dB. TVFool.com listed my location as "yellow" (which means use an attic antenna or higher). The cable drop is about 25 feet and I did not use an amplifier.

This antenna is supposed to be omni-directional but we did experience occasional signal drop on the networks with the initial "eyeball" installation (which was off about 15 degrees). Standing directly under the antenna and looking through a compass I had my son walk through the yard until he stepped into the path to the towers. Then I had him stand still, facing the antenna, and rotated it until he told me it was pointed straight over his head. That seemed to fix the signal drops. Given all the factors of our situation, I am probably maxing out the performance of this antenna. If I have any issues I'll just buy the add-on the reflector shield to increase directional performance...but for right now I don't need it.

Installation was easy (I just mounted it to the Direct TV mast). This antenna is small and light which was a big plus when climbing up a 25 foot ladder.

So far so good!
text_fidelity_b: Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Scosche MP12V MagicMount Magnetic Phone/GPS Power Outlet Mount for the Car I only purchased a smartphone about a year ago, previously being in the flip-phone-for-life crowd, due to the requirements of a job I was on. Since then I have slowly been picking up the various accouterments of such devices, the latest being this magnetic mount. I bought it mostly so I can use Google Maps for navigation.

It is remarkably effective. I have a Motorola Moto X4, in a slim silicon case, and an 05 Subaru Outback. The kit comes with the magnetic mount, two metal plates with adhesive (a rectangular one and a little circular one), a clear adhesive interposer, and, as a nice surprise, an alternate, black bezel.

What you do is attach the metal plate to the outside of your case, the inside of your case, or your phone. If you choose the lattermost option, then you don't attach it directly to the phone, but to the clear adhesive interposer (just a clear plastic sheet with adhesive on both sides), likely to prevent surface damage and dampen shock/reduce possible strain. If you have one of those pop-socket devices, you attach the little metal circle to the center of that instead. Then, you fit the magnetic mount to one of the grilles of your car's vent system, wherever it is most convenient. Now you can mount your phone to it, the magnet clinging to the metal plate.

I attached the metal plate to the inside of my case. It is very thin - I would say 1mm or less - and even on my slim silicon case it leaves only a very slight rise, hardly visible from the outside. I also attached it about 2/5ths of the way up from the bottom of the phone, as recommended (the Moto X4 does not have wireless charging). The magnet adheres quite well to the phone - the silicon case actually slightly pulls away when detaching the phone from the mount - not nearly enough to dislodge the case, but enough to let you know that the magnet is really sticking. As the mount has a rubber pad, and my case has a rubber texture, the phone does not slide at all in any lateral direction, the shear resistance is quite high. I am not concerned about the phone just falling off during normal operation of the car.

The tines of the mount grip the vents quite well - I have only had the mount pull off the vents once when detaching the phone after parking. There are two sizes of gaps - narrow and wide - and the narrow gap seems to fit pretty well on the Subaru. I like how you can pivot the mount a little to the left or right, and use the vent's own hinge to pivot it up and down.

There are some basic shortcomings of design. Obviously you can only attach this to the vents of the car, which limits your choice of positioning. I tried putting it on the left vent, but that caught too many outside reflections. I tried the right vent, but my hand was mostly blocking the screen. I tried the left passenger-side vent, but found that this took my eyes too far off the road while checking the navigation. In the end, I went with the driver's side right vent, since it required the lease eye-movement to check navigation and it was actually helpful to have my had block the screen, so as to avoid distraction. The tines hold, but they are not as secure as a hard mount would be. Likewise, the magnet could, in theory, be bumped out of position by kids/pets/carelessness and fall down into the foot well.

However, I would generally recommend this, at least as someone's first mount, to get a feel for what they are looking for if nothing else.
text_fidelity_b: Scosche MP12V MagicMount Magnetic Phone/GPS Power Outlet Mount for the Car

TOPROAD Portable Shower Speaker, IPX7 Waterproof Wireless Outdoor Speaker with HD Sound, 2 Suction Cups, Built-in Mic, Hands-Free Speakerphone for Bathroom, Pool, Beach, Hiking, Bicycle I have had several water resistant shower speakers and none, not one, my $600 Samsung Galaxy phone isn't. . . nothing is waterPROOF. It's a lie. Many advertisers and sellers like to claim waterproof status but what they mean is water RESISTANT. IPX7 means a device can survive immersion, up to 1 meter (3 ft 3 in) depth for up to 30 minutes. Let's also be clear here; those tests were with pure, likely purified, filtered water not highly chlorinated pool water. Not salty sea water. Not brackish lake/pond/river water. And also not water containing soaps, shampoos and conditioners. All that. . . stuff in every day water is going to reduce the effectiveness of the water resistance of any device.
So, I unbox this and it's light. Lighter than just about any speaker I've used. I look at the specs. . . 3 watts. THREE watts of power? Okay it's supposed to be primarily used in a small enclosed indoor space but it also says it's great for camping, hiking and general outdoors stuff (please, don't blast music when you're hiking, wear headphones, show some respect and restraint). I've never seen a non-novelty speaker that was less than 5 watts. It feels light and cheap and thin. The suction cups; they send two likely expecting one to fail. Neither worked. The best I could get with the cup wet with soapy water, alone, no speaker, stuck to a mirror for maybe five minutes. I can't get these suction cups to stick to my desk. No worries, my shower has a shelf. I turned off my oontz Angle 3 and connected this to my phone using Samsung Music as a player to take advantage of the Dolby Atmos and excellent sound (only PowerAmp sounded better of the half dozen players I tested and PowerAmp is a paid app only) quality it offers. I guess if you wanted noise in the shower this would work. Sound quality was about as bad as you'd expect. Distorted bass, harsh highs, muddy midrange. No EQ settings I tried made this sound good. It's just not worth it. You can for just a little more money get far better sounding water resistant speakers. You should enjoy the music in your shower or bath not suffer with it.
text_fidelity_b: TOPROAD Portable Shower Speaker, IPX7 Waterproof Wireless Outdoor Speaker with HD Sound, 2 Suction Cups, Built-in Mic, Hands-Free Speakerphone for Bathroom, Pool, Beach, Hiking, Bicycle

Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder This is a good voice recorder. Whether you need it to record your voice memos, lectures, meetings, or discretely record your favorite spy, this will surely be a recorder you'll find many uses for.

It feels very secure in your hand, and has a comfortable feel and weight. It comes with a small pouch, which is nice. The record button is easy to find my sight or feel. The volume and forward/reverse buttons are on an outer button from the record button. Play and stop on the left and index and menu are on the right.

f1 and f2 buttons are primarily used for setting mic sensitivity and voice quality. Under Mic Sensitivity you can choose: Dictate (good for personal memos), Speech recognition (turns on when it hears voice), conversation (good for interviews or conversations, auto zoom (good for large areas where there may be close up voices and far voices), and lecture (good for lectures)

You can choose either low quality at 8kbps in Mp3 format to super high quality 192kbps in mp3. There is also a wave format in 1411 kbps. The higher quality you go impacts total record time. You can add a micro SD card for adding recording time.

There are also 4 index folders labeled A thru D. These are for separating projects. There is also a folder you could place music files if you wanted this to be a mp3 player.

There is also a menu setting where the voice quality and mic sensitivity can be accessed as well as numerous other options such as splitting files, display contrast, and clearvoice (an option that improves the sound quality of the recorded voiec)

The unit comes with rechargable AA batteries that will need to be charged when you first open it. They charge with the included usb to micro USB cord. Any other micro USB cord you own will also work. Once the recorder is connected to your computer through the USB cable you can download and upload voice or mp3 and wave files.

The only thing I wish this had was different settings for each index. For instance I would have liked to set index A for lecture mode at high quality, index B for dictate at a lower quality, etc. Once you set a mic sensitivity and recording quality, they are the same for all index until you change them in settings.

Overall a great quality recorder. Great for meetings, memos, and conversations.
text_fidelity_b: Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder

TP-Link AC750 Wifi Range Extender | Up to 750Mbps | Dual Band WiFi Extender, Repeater, Wifi Signal Booster, Access Point| Easy Set-Up | Extends Wifi to Smart Home & Alexa Devices (RE200) This review is for the TP-link AC750 Dual Band WiFi Range Extender

I am using this on a network that has a Mac Mini, a couple of iPhones and an iPad. None of these devices could print to both printers; it was one or the other and not both on every single Apple product. After trying everything I could think of, I bought this extender and tried to set it up using the Quick Setup instructions. Anyone EVER had the experience of those Quick Setups working? I haven't and I've been using this stuff for decades. After Quick Setup failed to do anything other than connect to my router and open my network up to anyone that could get signal, I tried a different approach.

The EASIEST WAY TO SET THIS UP is to use the WPS button on your router and on the device. Press the WPS button on the router, then, press the WPS button on the extender. After a minute or so, the router and extender are paired/connected and the result is a secure connection to the router (uses the router's password--you do have a password don't you) with a much stronger signal in what were dead zones. Placement of the extender is sort of an experiment and moving it from plug to plug will show you the best location. Moving the extender after pairing does NOT foul up the connection.

I have two printers, a Samsung M2070W laser and an Epson Eco Tank inkjet. Both have wireless capability and can use WPS setup. To setup other WPS capable devices, just press the WPS button on the ROUTER and then the WPS button on the next device you want to connect. The connection to the router goes through the connected extender with no problem and does not interfere with the router/extender pairing. Do each device one at a time.

This was the solution I needed and now all wireless devices work together. It's a neat solution to solving signal strength and connectivity that can be an enormous hassle when using multiple devices from different makers.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC750 Wifi Range Extender | Up to 750Mbps | Dual Band WiFi Extender, Repeater, Wifi Signal Booster, Access Point| Easy Set-Up | Extends Wifi to Smart Home & Alexa Devices (RE200)

Fast-forward two and a half years... My Nook was getting older and the discrepancy between prices and availability of e-books between Amazon and Barnes & Noble was becoming increasingly clearer. Also, I love Amazon as a general rule, and order from them pretty heavily for a variety of items, so it made sense to switch over. After brief research, I stumbled upon the Kindle Paperwhite. It met all of my requirements - a dedicated e-reader (no tablet for me, thanks), with a built in light. Yippee! My hubby and puppy (okay, just the hubby) purchased the Kindle Paperwhite for my birthday at the end of August and it was love at first sight. It is unreasonable to compare the Kindle Paperwhite to my old Nook, so I won't. I can freely admit that most of my love comes from the new technology and association with Amazon. I love the light. It is awesome to not have to use a clip on light at night. They are usually terrible and not evenly spaced. The light makes reading at night a breeze. Plus, it is a perfect light, so it really is like reading a book and not like reading on a backlit screen (a la the iPhone or iPad). I love the ease of purchasing books from Amazon, and I love their prices and special deals. But, most of all, I love checking out library books! The very thing that turned me away from the Kindle initially is now the best. There is no need to connect my Kindle to a laptop to download a book. Yay! I can just wirelessly send a book to my Kindle, the same as purchasing one. You must be a wireless network (not 3G), but that my dear friends is a tiny issue. Overall, I love my Kindle Paperwhite and I cannot think of one single thing to make it better! Love it.

Helpful tips - 3G or not? I love the 3G, but it's not a necessity if you have wide access to wireless. I would definitely say to go for the ads, however. They are entirely inoffensive and unobtrusive. They only come up when your Kindle is asleep. Save the $20 and buy yourself a few books!
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th]

Every one of the AmazonBasics branded items I’ve tested has been excellent and this cable is no exception.

Typically any device requiring an Ethernet cable will come with one in the packaging - it will work (usually). A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without fail.

This Cat7 is designed to be thin, but don’t let that fool you into thinking that it lacks capacity - within the thin PVC package contains aluminum shielding and 100% bare copper wires for super fast transfer speeds. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The plugs have a protective rubber boot guard that protects the clip on the plug - this becomes very important when snaking the cable through walls and tight spaces. Prior to doing this I wrap the boot and plug with a small piece of electrical tape to make sure I don’t unintentionally snag anything.

I love the white PVC shielding on this cable - not only is it durable and will help the cable withstand damage but it can be run along a wall and then painted to match the wall color.

I used this 25 foot cable to run between my router to a unmanaged switch that branches to several IoT hubs - a primary connection where speed and a reliable relay is critical - and I’ve been nothing but impressed by this product.

You will not find a better Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love. This is a purchase that you’ll never regret.
